name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish). The dataset includes transcribed audio segments, language models, and baseline ASR models for all languages.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: Audio data was downloaded from LibriVox audiobooks using data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. All audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text sources for audiobooks were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org for English. For other languages, text extraction involved both automated parsers and manual approaches including copying text from browsers, extracting from PDF/EPUB files using pdftotext, and writing HTML parsers for popular domains. For audiobooks with invalid links, manual searches were conducted to find alternative sources.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio data sourced from LibriVox audiobooks (read audiobooks in the public domain). Text data sourced from Project Gutenberg books and other public domain sources including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, projekt-gutenberg.de, zeno.org, and spiegel.de.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels to handle variations in number pronunciation. Heuristics were applied to handle hyphens and apostrophes: rare words with hyphens or apostrophes were replaced based on frequency thresholds (words appearing in fewer than a chosen threshold of distinct books). End-of-line hyphens were removed and word parts joined into single words.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. Segmentation was performed by running inference to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then splitting at the longest silence duration within 10-20 second ranges. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges based on language orthography. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or dramatic readings were removed. Only the latest version of books sharing the same authors and title were kept. Speakers with duration shorter than a threshold were assigned to training set. Language model corpus was filtered to avoid overlap with dev/test sets using edit distance on titles and 5-gram matching.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were retrieved through an automated alignment process: pseudo labels were generated using beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models on trained acoustic models. Source text was split into overlapping documents of 1250 words (striding by 1000 words). Documents were retrieved using TF-IDF similarity score on bigrams, followed by Smith-Waterman alignment to find best matching sub-sequences. Candidate transcripts with WER >40% compared to pseudo labels were filtered out. For development and test sets, human transcribers listened to audio while viewing transcripts and were asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to ensure high quality without introducing bias.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss for segmentation and pseudo-label generation. wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference. Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm for transcript matching. Gender classifier: SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech data consuming 40-dimensional log-filterbank features.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender information was collected for speakers using an automated gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel) to ensure balanced gender distribution in development and test sets.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read-speech only, derived from audiobooks, which may limit generalization to conversational or spontaneous speech. For Polish, the language model has a high out-of-vocabulary (OOV) rate of 13.39%, which negatively impacts ASR performance when using constrained lexicon decoding. The diversity of text source domains for non-English languages made automated text extraction challenging, requiring manual intervention. Some audiobooks had invalid or redirected links for text sources. The pseudo-label based transcript retrieval process may introduce errors where the pseudo labels are incorrect.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. It can be used for training, validation, and testing of ASR models. Limited supervision subsets (10-hour, 1-hour, and six 10-minute sets) are provided for low-resource training benchmarks. The dataset enables research in large-scale multilingual ASR training. For English, the training set is interchangeable and complementary with LibriSpeech, with completely independent development and test sets.
